fix_commit_message:
openssl: skip session resumption when verifystatus is set

Resumed TLS sessions skip OCSP stapled-response verification.
Force a full handshake so verifystatus() runs.

Closes #18902
agent_reasoning: Without this guard, ossl_connect_step1() still looks up and installs a cached session ID even when conn_config->verifystatus is set, and servercert() already skips verifystatus() whenever connssl->reused_session is TRUE. The combination means a handle configured with CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYSTATUS could silently reuse a prior TLS session (e.g. on a second request to the same host) and never check the OCSP stapled response for that connection, defeating revocation checking. The fix adds `&& !conn_config->verifystatus` to the sessionid-lookup condition in ossl_connect_step1, so a full handshake (and therefore verifystatus()) is forced whenever OCSP-stapling verification is requested.
